results.description: You’ve been travelling for some time now and have seen so much, it’s been great but you’re feeling like you could slow down a bit. You also feel like being pampered and indulging… and you’ve considered the famous Middle Estern hammams…but you don’t feel completely comfortable with the idea…I get it and I got your back. results.name: Visit Qatayef Bakeries
results.description: The Qatayef dessert is one of the most important official sweets served during Ramadan. Almost every Jordanian household serves Qatayef for Ifatr during Ramadan. We will take you on a tour in the streets of Amman and we will visit the most famous bakeries that produce qatayef before Iftar. Qatayef production goes through  4 different stages: the first step consists of preparing the dough and baking it,  the second stage is stuffing the qatayef with different fillings (some like dates or nuts, while some prefer cheese or cream, and some, more recently, stuff the qatayef with Nutella). The third stage is that of frying the stuffed qatayef, while the final stage  is dipping the qatayef in honey. The final product is a true delight to the taste buds. You will see all these stages during your visit to the Qatayef shops in Ramadan, and you will taste the most delicious varieties of Qatayef. Please note: Price does not include food, drinks, tickets or transportation.

results.name: Fasten your seatbelt! Oh there is not any! It’s an Auto Rickshaw Tour!
results.description: Do you think you have experienced the weirdest transportation? Please rethink again! In Egypt, you can find all types of modes, including horse and carriage, and donkey. Your experience will not be completed with auto rickshaw. It became the primary way to move between narrow lanes in the urban slums. You will want to record this moment and get access to local spots to explore the daily life of Egyptians. You will never get hungry in Egypt. Why? Because you will find vendors, food carts, and more. They offer everything you can imagine. You want to taste all and discover what street food in Egypt is all about. We don’t blame you. The air is loaded with irresistible aroma and you want to partake in what locals eat every day. But what if you’re going out to explore only delicious street food to avoid any digestive problems and find out historical food trucks and worthy local small vendor, you need to be accompanied with a local. Please note: Price does not include food, drinks, tickets or transportation.

results.name: Watch a Timeless Arabic Film: Cinema Zawya
results.description: There is no better way to understand a country’s culture than watching movies. But it’s not just like any other movie theater. Cinema Zawya is a cultural center where you can find people from around the world who are fascinated about classic movies just like you. We are Egyptians and we know what you’d like to watch and what is considered time-wasting. All movies come with English subtitles. So, after watching a really good Arabic movie, you will join a group discussion to share with others what you think and strike questions to dig deeper in Egyptian culture, and know more about Egyptian superstars who framed the Arabic cinema scene. So, let’s have an authentic movie night in the heart of Cairo! Please note: Price does not include food, drinks, tickets or transportation.

results.name: My One and Only Place I Go Every Time Without Boring (A Normal Day of an Egyptian Guy)
results.description: Let's venture to a Qahwa, a traditional café that is typically found on the streets of Egypt. Qahwas are considered the ultimate safe haven for Egyptian men. Whether they're looking to catch an important sports match, sip on a cup of coffee or tea, or simply enjoy a good laugh and quality time with their buddies, Qahwas are the go-to spot. Not just that, everyone has its preferred Qahwa and they can’t change it under any circumstances. What's more, Qahwas are one of the most affordable ways to enjoy oneself. Even if you don't order anything, no one will ask you to leave. You're cordially invited to partake in this authentic local experience, where you can witness firsthand how Egyptian men spend their evenings. Engage in a game of tables, one of the traditional games, or strike up a conversation with some of the humorous locals. Please note: Price does not include food, drinks, tickets or transportation.

results.name: Have Traditional Suhoor in Ramadan on The Most Popular Foul Cart in Egypt
results.description: In Egypt’s Suhoor is an experience in itself. It’s the last meal Muslims eat during Ramadan, before the sunrise or Alfajr prayer. Since Ramadan is only month each year, Egyptians have their own rituals during the Suhoor. What’s more imagine you have this meal in one of the oldest districts in Cairo on the most popular foul cart in Egypt, Waheed Cart. You will get the most authentic Ramadan vibes around Cairo, eating traditional dishes, chatting, snapping away, and more. Exciting, right! Please note: Price does not include food, drinks, tickets or transportation.

Have a good knowledge of Amman and the locations of the large mosques that perform Taraweeh prayers daily.
results.name: Tarawih Prayer
results.description: Tarawih prayer, one of the most important religious and spiritual rituals in the holy month of Ramadan, is something worth experiencing. Muslims perform Tarawih prayers immediately after the Isha (evening) prayer each day during the month of Ramadan.  They pray to God, ask forgiveness, recite the Qur'an, and connect to their Creator and to each other.  If you are a Muslim, you can perform this prayer with the worshipers in any of the mosques in Jordan. If you are not a Muslim, you can observe the praying crowd in the mosque. The energy of the place will captivate you, after all, we can all use a little meditation from time to time..  After the Tarawih prayer, on their way home, some people stop by the bustling markets to buy food, some  go to the cafes to stay up late and enjoy  the night, while  some go home to watch the Ramadan series…and some stay in the mosques and continue praying and reading the Qur’an. Please note: Price does not include food, drinks, tickets or transportation.
